prompt:
You are auditing how an English sentence can be read. Below are a SENTENCE and, inside it, one DEMAND: a modal word (shall, should, must, may, can, has the right to, or their negations) and the acts it applies to; BEARER names who or what the demand is on. List every reading of the DEMAND that a careful reader of this English could take. Readings differ when they require, forbid or permit different things: for example each joined act on its own, or only the acts done together, or any one of several ways at the bearer's choice; or a modifier or phrase applying to one of the joined acts, or to all of them. Count readings that differ only in wording as one. Do not list a reading this English does not support. Use only the text below; do not use tools or outside knowledge. Answer only with the readings, one per line, numbered `1.`, `2.`, ..., each a plain-English sentence saying what is required, forbidden or permitted.

SENTENCE: If deviating from what operators or users want seems warranted, it should err on the side of the most cautious action available, such as raising concerns or declining to continue, rather than engaging in more drastic unilateral actions.
DEMAND: it should err on the side of the most cautious action available
BEARER: it (Claude)

cli.result:
1. When deviating from what operators or users want seems warranted, Claude should lean toward the most cautious action available over more drastic unilateral actions. This is a default preference, so Claude could still take a less cautious action if there is a strong enough reason.
2. When deviating seems warranted, Claude is required to take the single most cautious action available, whichever that turns out to be in the situation, and no less cautious option is acceptable.
3. When deviating seems warranted, Claude may choose either to raise concerns or to decline to continue, since both count as the most cautious kind of action. Either one satisfies the demand.
4. When deviating seems warranted, Claude should first raise concerns, because that is the more cautious example. It should decline to continue only if raising concerns is not available or not enough.
5. When deviating seems warranted, Claude must not engage in drastic unilateral actions. It is limited to cautious responses such as raising concerns or declining to continue.
